relatedEvidence.term: what is a meander in geography

demand.selection: Use meander definition plus erosion/oxbow explanation, rather than claim exact why-do-rivers-meander demand. Use QWERTY meaning, typewriter history and uncertainty, excluding broad keyboard shopping/device terms and keysmash queries.
demand.limits: Normalised sampled relative interest, not absolute searches, search difficulty, international totals or promised visits. The two articles are written in English for an international audience, but the observed market is the US only. Zeros do not prove no searches.

intent.readerNeed: Define the feature quickly, explain why the shape moves and recognise an abandoned loop without a long school-style worksheet.
intent.serpObserved: Searches for why do rivers meander and USGS meander return explanatory geography pages, school materials, USGS educational/research records and oxbow discussions. Root's native Trends refinement selects the supported definition intent rather than the unmeasured exact why query.

competingExamples.type: Official educational definition; discovery result reviewed but direct opening timed out; excluded from article citations
Long explanatory geography result; not used as a factual source
Official satellite-image explainer; opened and cited

intent.ownDifference: 215-word accessible explanation, two-bank contrast, actual USGS time-series link and one connected salinity read; no unsupported universal claim that all rivers develop the same shape.

intent.readerNeed: Explain the odd name and inherited layout while distinguishing evidence from the familiar oversimplified slow-typists story.
intent.serpObserved: Exact question returns WSU's fresh historian interview, innovation histories, commercial keyboard/typing blogs and explanatory videos. Broad qwerty keyboard queries also contain device shopping intent; excluded from selection.

competingExamples.type: Museum historical explainer; discovery text available, direct fetch forbidden; excluded from article citations
Typing tool blog; search-result intent only, not a factual source

intent.ownDifference: Short original explanation uses an inspected original 1878 patent drawing and explicit uncertainty, without claiming that QWERTY was certainly designed to slow typing or that it is the best layout.

checkedSources.title: Ground Water Atlas of the United States, Segment 5 — Surficial aquifer system
checkedSources.type: Government scientific explanation based on Mississippi alluvial geology
checkedSources.opening: Web browser fetch returned 403, but independent Python HTTPS GET returned 200. Full HTML and parsed text saved and exact paragraph read. This is not a claim that the web fetch succeeded.
supports: Meandering streams shift by eroding the outside of bends and depositing sediment on the inside of downstream bends
A cutoff shortens the channel and can leave a crescent-shaped oxbow lake
bounds: No numerical meander migration rate asserted
No claim that every river meanders
No one-force explanation of all river shapes
No river safety or engineering guidance

checkedSources.title: Oxbow Lakes
checkedSources.type: Government observation with dated Landsat image series
checkedSources.opening: Web tool opened full page and independent HTTPS GET returned 200. Full HTML and text saved.
supports: A meander can form a cutoff leaving a separate oxbow lake
Dated imagery explicitly identifies the Mamoré River in Bolivia, including images from 1984 through 2023
Curved water bodies beside the channel can mark old bends
bounds: Cover is conceptual, not an illustration of the Mamoré
No claim oxbow lakes remain permanently unchanged

checkedSources.title: Why are the keyboard keys not in ABC order?
checkedSources.type: Firsthand interview with librarian and trained historian Erin Hvizdak
checkedSources.opening: Web tool opened full article and independent HTTPS GET returned 200. Full HTML and parsed text saved.
supports: QWERTY name comes from top-row letters
Slow-typing/jamming account is questioned and telegraph-operator explanation discussed
Familiarity contributed to persistence into computers
bounds: Competing explanations attributed as explanations, not established fact
No claim QWERTY is faster, better or the only keyboard
No unsupported learning-speed or ergonomic claims

checkedSources.publisher: Original US Patent Office patent, hosted by Google Patents
checkedSources.title: C. Latham Sholes — Improvement in type-writing machines, US207559
checkedSources.opening: Google Patents page and seven-page PDF opened in web tool; actual PDF downloaded via HTTPS200; page2 rendered using Poppler and visually inspected. OCR is imperfect, so date, inventor and Fig3 lettering checked against drawing.
supports: Figure3 top letter row starts QWERTY; other details differ from modern keyboard, so article avoids saying identical
Description of key/type movement, printing against inking substance and paper, and letter-space movement
bounds: Patent is evidence of layout and mechanics, not proof of intention
No claim this is the first keyboard or first patent
Original figure not reused as cover artwork
